messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm proposing a compactification of the console ingest schema to cut the per-route telemetry storage footprint. Need quick sync on quotas, routing, and dashboard fallbacks.

sam: Short question — which fields are we removing or moving? need to reason about query fallbacks.

maria: Plan sketch: move high-cardinality route_attrs map into a separate denormalized table (route_attr_keys) and keep a compact route_signatures blob for the console hot-path. Dual-write new schema alongside existing for 2w. Backfill only hourly aggregates for >30d to avoid huge replay.

ben: Concern — alerting drilldowns depend on route_attrs. If we compact, dashboards that drill to attr-level will break for older windows. UX idea: show a "expanded attrs unavailable for this time window" banner and link to aggregated breakdown. @elaine?

elaine: Agree on the banner. Also we should add provenance metadata to each timeseries (live vs aggregated) and expose attr_resolution_version in the telemetry contract so callers can opt into the more expensive join.

kai: @maria what's the migration window and backfill plan? We need to avoid quota calculation spikes and coordinate with billing exports.

maria: Canary plan: 10% tenants weekend canary -> 48h monitor -> ramp if healthy. Backfill will be an incremental hourly worker writing denorm rows; estimated 18h per region for historical 90d horizon but we'll throttle to keep DB iowait and quota usage low.

ben: Routing note: read-adapter should prefer the compact index and only fallback to legacy storage if a join is needed. That keeps p99 down. We'll gate with a feature flag.

sam: Feature flag + read-adapter makes sense. Also propose read-path exposes meta attr_status so programmatic clients can know if they got full attrs. Avoid returning 202s.

elaine: Agreed, hide 202. UI shows "partial attrs" state. API returns { meta: { attr_status: "partial|complete" } } so SDKs can surface the banner.

maria: Finalized plan for now: dual-write -> read-adapter prefers new table -> UI shows partial notice when needed -> backfill -> switch default read to new table after 2w if no regressions. We'll also create a migration runbook.

kai: Quota calc impact: if read-adapter adds joins, route those queries to a cached denorm path. Add an observability dashboard for quota p95/p99 on canary tenants and an alert for any >15% latency regression.

ben: :thumbsup: Also add a regression alert for cost-per-query for telemetry endpoints.

elaine: Who owns the backfill runbook and oncall play? Ops or eng-platform?

maria: I'll own the runbook; ops will run the heavy lifting. I'll post the draft runbook here: https://ourwiki.local/migrations/console-compactify (stub).

sam: Add rollback steps: stop dualwrite, revert read-adapter config, and a controlled replay to revert denorm rows if we need to abort. DB migrations need CONCURRENT index builds and a preflight to estimate time.

maria: Rollback checklist included: 1) pause backfill 2) switch read-adapter to legacy 3) mark migration aborted in audit log 4) cleanup indexes as necessary. We'll enforce index create as CONCURRENT and run preflight queries to estimate index time.

kai: Can we aim for next Friday 02:00 UTC canary? I'll reserve the maintenance window and monitor rotation.

maria: Yes — scheduling for next Friday 02:00 UTC. I'll post a detailed checklist in #eng-platform later today.

ben: Small nit — keep billing exports on legacy canonical fields until billing confirms parity. We shouldn't surprise the billing pipeline.

elaine: I'll loop in billing (cc @tom) to validate parity.

deploy-bot: Feature flag created: console.compactify.v1 (id: ff-789) — created by maria.

maria: Thanks all — I'll update the checklist and follow up with a short RFC with schema DDLs and cost estimates.
